title: Internal Communication Guideline
note: Document code prefix is GL- (guideline), not ML- (manual). Section 01 does NOT follow the X.1 Purpose/X.2 Scope pattern used elsewhere - its sub-topics are plain prose headings.

nodes.heading: Purpose
nodes.own_text:
This document aims to build the employees capacity on an effective
communication practice by providing them with general guidelines and
professional practices on internal communication. For this purpose, this document
covers more specific details on benefits of effective internal communication, main
principles of effective internal communication, and the steps required for effective
communication. It also highlights the major obstacles in communication and how
to overcome them through considering the importance of communications in
diverse work groups. It also shed the light on the essential communication
channels which are broadly used at GHD|EMPHNET and needed by the
employees to communicate with different parties internally. Furthermore, this
document provides employees with the needed information to manage information
flow with stakeholders in a more efficient and effective manner.
This document targets all teams at HQ and Country Offices and, to some extent
with external parties. Additionally, it describes the planned and periodic
communication occurring between different internal communications platforms.
Hence, the ultimate purpose of this document is to guide the implementation of
GHD|EMPHNET operations, and it defines information that needs to be
communicated between GHD|EMPHNET divisions, teams, and units.

nodes.heading: Responsibility
nodes.own_text:
y
GHD|EMPHNET is committed to ensuring that appropriate policies, procedures, and
monitoring arrangements are in place to support good internal communications at HQ
and Country Offices. On the other hand, employees should communicate effectively
to enhance the productive working environment and ensure success in delivering
GHD|EMPHNET’s operational goals and plans.
Managers, Team Leaders, and Directors are responsible to ensure implementation of
effective communication within their teams and other teams. They should create an
open and informative culture where all employees are encouraged to seek and give
information.
Employees are responsible to follow the principles and steps of effective
communication, share information in a timely manner, and seek information that is
relevant to their work.
EMPHNET’s Executive Director has the responsibility to approve and sign this
guideline according to the endorsed authority matrix.
The Quality Management team is responsible for performing regular reviews and
monitoring progress, in order to identify possible risks and to guarantee that all
measures are taken to prevent the breaching of policies and/or procedures.
GHD|EMPHNET has the right to amend this guideline at any time. Failure to comply
with the policies or instructions mentioned in this document could result in disciplinary
action up to and including suspension or termination.

nodes.path: Section 01 > Benefits of Effective Internal Communication
nodes.heading: Benefits of Effective Internal Communication
nodes.next_heading: Main Principles of Effective Internal Communication
nodes.own_text:
Effective internal communication between all internal participants i.e. employees,
management, or consultants, creates a cohesive culture where everyone is
focused on the same goals. By working within a cohesive culture, different teams
can work more efficiently, and they can collaborate more effectively. Some specific
benefits that can result from effective internal communication include:
•
Internal Brand Awareness: to ensure that all employees are aware of the
organization’s mission and vision.
•
Employee Engagement: to keep all employees abreast with all
organizational
updates,
news,
achievements,
new
projects,
and
partnerships, etc.
•
Enabling Change within the Organization: to enable and empower all
employees to make decisions themselves by having the tools and
knowledge they need to make decisions that are in line with the
organization’s goals.
•
Building a Culture of Open Communication: to provide a number of
channels and platforms for all teams to share useful resources and
information, to lessen duplication of work and to strengthen impact.
•
Driving Organizational Performance: to reduce the day-to-day conflict
since conflicts usually are the result of different opinions on what is
important to the organization.
•
Build an Organizational Culture: Where people work together effectively
towards a common goal.

nodes.path: Section 01 > Main Principles of Effective Internal Communication
nodes.heading: Main Principles of Effective Internal Communication
nodes.own_text:
Ineffective internal communication is usually either arbitrary or incomplete or
planned only in reaction to specific events. However, Effective internal
communication should be always planned, not only to deal with specific issues, but
for the well-being of the organization, in the long run.
In this document, some basic principles need to be adopted to ensure effective
internal communication across the organization.
These include;
•
Long-term focus
•
Values to be clearly communicated.
•
Communication strategy is crucial for successful and effective internal
communication.
•
Consistency in spreading messages.
•
Being proactive
•
Creating and maintaining a positive image.
•
Tailored to the audience (both in delivery and content)
•
Communicating in timely manner

While communication and disseminating work related messages and information on a
timely basis is essential for work success, confidentiality and privacy aspects of some
data and information should be taken into consideration during the work dissemination.

nodes.path: Section 01 > Three-Step Process for Effective Communication
nodes.heading: Three-Step Process for Effective Communication
nodes.note: internally covers Identify Communication Requirements / Identify the 5Ws and 1H / Identify and Accommodate the Enterprise Environmental Factors - kept as one leaf, no separate TOC entries
nodes.own_text:
Identify Communication Requirements
Employee should know what the requirements of successful communications are to
plan on how to achieve those requirements. He/she should first identify who needs
what information. Stakeholders need different types of information, depending on their
interest and priority. Besides, it is essential to determine the channels of
communication, how often the information is needed, involved departments, the
number of individuals involved, etc. and that there are no gaps in everyone's'
understanding.
Identify the 5Ws (Why, What, When, Where, Who) and 1H (How)
Identify the 5Ws (Why, What, When, Where, Who) and 1H (How) is one of the methods
that used to assist in identifying communication requirements as the following:
• Who needs to be communicated to.
• What needs to be communicated taking into consideration the confidentiality
and privacy aspects.
• When it should be communicated, and the timeline of communication should
be monitored.
• Where should it be communicated. If the team involves many people, then
individual level and team level communications needs to be resolved.
• Why communication of information is essential and to what level is important.
• How the communication needs to be done; via e-mail, phone, etc.
Figure 1: The 5 “W's” and 1 “H”

Identify and Accommodate the Enterprise Environmental Factors and
Organizational Process Assets
Much of the day-day communication is linked to the enterprise environmental factors
and Organizational Process Assets. All employees should review and identify these
factors and assets to ensure effective communication. These includes:
• Organizational culture and structure,
•
Standard, regulations, policies, and procedures,
•
The logistics and the organizational infrastructure,
•
The human resources,
•
The authorization matrix,
•
Information system.
•
Workflow and instructions for example the Business Automation System
•
Organization templates for example reports, biweekly meetings minutes,
etc.

nodes.heading: Major Challenges in Communication
nodes.own_text:
Employees at GHD|EMPHNET are working through different interfaces such as
different departments, different organizations, country offices. Therefore, it is very
essential to understand major challenges that limit effective communication between
different interfaces at GHD|EMPHNET and to try to overcome. Many issues can arise
such as differences of opinion and miss-understandings. Involved employees need to
be aware of the differences, understand the divergences in attitudes between the
involved parties, and then act as intermediaries to facilitate communication.

nodes.heading: 2.1.1 Microsoft Teams
nodes.own_text:
Audience
Headquarters and Country Offices employees and External
Stakeholders as needed
Purpose
A unified communication and collaboration platform that
combines persistent workplace messaging, video meetings,
file storage, and application integration. It is a collaboration
environment for the team, that can be used to:
➢ Discuss with the team using posts and chat box.
➢ Meet with the team using the audio, visual, and share
screen features.
➢ Share files and store them in folders.
➢ Chat with or call anyone in the organization.
Best For
MS Teams is considered the first choice platforms for
meetings conduct at GHD|EMPHNET
Internal Meetings (bi-weekly, team meetings, one-to-one,
etc.)
External Meetings (regular meetings with funders and
partners,
one-to-one
with
geographically
located
stakeholders)
Responsibility
➢ Ensure that involved parties have Microsoft Teams
installed.
➢ Number of participants are limited, (1,000 participants).

General rules for using Microsoft Teams:
Employees shall respond to received messages and calls immediately, if this
was not applicable, the user shall respond within 24 hours.
Attendees shall be informed before recording any meeting.
Opening cameras is mandatory in planned meetings.
Meetings should be arranged using Outlook Meeting Requests:
o
When organizing a meeting, check availability by viewing colleagues’
calendars or by using the Outlook Scheduling Assistant within a Meeting
Request.
o
When you receive a meeting request, you should accept, reject, or
suggest a more suitable time as soon as possible in order to help the
person arranging the meeting.
o
Keep your Outlook calendar up-to-date by entering appointments and
holidays with the correct availability setting so others can check and see
your availability for meetings and collaborative work.
o
Share your calendar with others to display your appointments. If you do
change the privacy setting to ‘None’ this will automatically be reverted to
Free/Busy.
o
Share your calendar with your team so they can see your appointments.
o
For part-time staff, create recurring appointments to show when you are
not normally working. If you normally finish work at 2:00 pm on a
Wednesday, set up a recurring appointment 2:00 – 5:30 pm every
Wednesday and set the availability to Out of Office with the subject ‘Non-
working time’.
o
You may block out time to focus on a particular piece of work. This can be
marked as ‘Tentative’ so meeting organizers will try to avoid arranging
meetings during this time but may use it if there are no other options.

nodes.heading: 2.1.2 Zoom
nodes.own_text:
Audience
Specific employees requesting to webinars, workshops, etc.
Purpose
It provides videotelephony and online chat services through
a cloud-based peer-to-peer software platform and is used
for teleconferencing and telecommuting.
Best For
Webinars, workshops for multi-geographies, etc.
Responsibility
➢ Number of participants are limited, (100 participants for
meeting and 1,000 for webinar).

General Instructions for using Zoom:
Send your request a good time before the meeting to the Technology and
Innovative Solutions in order to give them the appropriate time to arrange for
your request among other meetings.
If requested by the meeting organizer, a representative from Technology and
Innovative solution shall be available during the meeting to provide the required
support, otherwise one of the meeting attendees will be assigned as the host.
Meetings should be arranged using Outlook Meeting Requests and the Zoom
link shall be shared within the meeting request.

nodes.heading: 2.2 Face-to-Face Meeting
nodes.own_text:
Audience
Headquarters and Country Offices Employees and External
Stakeholders as needed
Purpose
Face-to-face meeting is still the best communication as it is
direct and two-way communication and allows the
discussion of sensitive issues that require more nuance
derived from body language and direct interaction. It is the
ideal medium for holding discussions on important issues
and getting feedback from audience in an immediate
manner. In addition, it can also be more informal and have
more social aspects than many other forms.
Best For
All meetings were all audience are located in the same area
or can be easily gathered in the same area, where body
language plays a vital role to deliver the message alongside
the direct interaction i.e. capacity building workshops,
interviews, etc.
Responsibility
Meeting requester
➢ If further support is needed to set the meeting room for
Technology related issues, please refer to the
Technology and Innovative Solutions team.
➢ Meetings can be held in a hybrid mode, both face-face
and virtual, required support shall be requested from the
Technology and Innovative Solutions team to make the
required arrangements.
General Instructions for face-to-face meetings:
All meetings should be arranged using Outlook Meeting Requests.
Meeting rooms shall be booked before the meeting to assure availability. The
meeting location shall be specified in the meeting request.

Technology and Innovative Solutions team shall make the required support for
technology solutions such as mics, screens, etc.

nodes.path: Section 02 > 2.3 Emails > Email subject and writing style
nodes.heading: Email subject and writing style
nodes.own_text:
o Work email addresses are to be used strictly for business. It is not
allowed to use your email account for personal use.
o Emails, when possible, should be kept concise, clear and to the point
avoiding irrelevant text. Paragraphs should be kept short, using bullet
points where possible.
o The body of the email should be in font Calibri 11pt. Backgrounds are
not allowed in emails. Make sure that text is left aligned when composing
emails in English and right aligned for emails in Arabic. Same goes for
text direction (left-to-right for English and right-to-left for Arabic).
o Do not use any emoji or funny characters/symbols. Keep the email
language professional. Email’s subject should be clear and concise, so
it is easy to find again in inboxes.
o The email should clarify whether it is sent for action or information and
what is expected of the recipient and by when.
o The email should, if any action is required, highlight this in the text,
stating by whom and when. Use paragraph settings to break ideas,
information, or thoughts.
o Do not change the subject on long email chains/thread.
o Always include the standard email signature in any new emails that you
send. Including an email signature in the “Reply to” and “forward” emails
is not essential unless sent externally.
o It is encouraged to embed links by inserting hyperlinks over relevant text.

o All-user emails are tightly regulated and are only sent for issues of
institutional importance. The Executive Director, Communication,
Technology, Knowledge and Exchange, Quality Management, Finance
and Human Resources are the only parties with permission to send all
employees, unless the need is set and demanded by the Executive
Director.
o Use asterisks * around a word or bold a word to add emphasis, if needed.
o Proofread the email and ensure spell checker is activated.
o Try not to use abbreviations such as TBD (to be decided), especially
when emailing external parties. In business emails these are generally
not appropriate.
o Address recipients with “Dear XXX”. Do not use “Dears” without a name
that follows. You can use “Dear All” when sending to more than one
recipient.
o If multiple and different actions needed in the same email from multiple
employees use “@” to assign the task to the relevant person.

nodes.heading: Reply and Forward
nodes.own_text:
o Initial replies to emails should be within the same day if received during
the official working hours and within 24 hours if sent outside the working
hours. When action is required from an email, reply by acknowledging
receipt of the email and requested action and highlight a timeline for
sending the requested information. This applies to internal and well as
external emails.
o When replying, do not send a "reply to all" unless it is necessary for all
copied recipients to know your response.
o If an email is addressed to more than one person, call that other person
to agree on the reply or action needed.
o When forwarding or replying to emails, follow the same rules as you
would for initiating an email, e.g. make clear to whom you are sending
the email and what action is needed. Also make sure that the subject is
an appropriate one.
o Do not use an email with a subject heading to introduce or follow up on
a separate subject. Start a new email with a new subject line.
o When you are out of the office for more than two days, use “out of office
auto message reply option” and ensure that the message includes the
dates or times you are unavailable for, and an alternative contact for
urgent queries.
o Directors, Team Leaders, and Managers leaving the office for annual
vacations or business leaves for more than two working days inside or
outside Jordan, are kindly requested to inform GHD|EMPHNET teams
via email clearly stating the dates on which they will be absent, and they
should also specify who will be acting on their behalf. Also, if applicable,
Team Leaders, Directors, and Managers are also requested to delegate
their authority and responsibilities on BAS with this change.

o Replying to the emails should be always by direct receiver, anyone on
the cc should not reply directly unless direct action from his/her end is
needed or if that copied person is the direct manager or in a higher
hierarchical position. It is preferable to obtain prior approval before
responding directly to emails specially if the direct receiver is your direct
manager.

nodes.heading: Recipients
nodes.own_text:
o Emails should be sent directly to the person they are intended for. Make
sure that all others are in the cc.
o Do not copy anyone in ‘just in case’. Emails addressed to recipients
should always be on a need-to-know basis or requiring action or advice.
Therefore, emails should be sent "to" people who in turn are to take
some kind of action while "cc" is for people who need to know about this.
o You can always forward an email to a recipient if you need to inform that
recipient, rather than copy.
o If an email thread gets long and the information in the email
communication becomes irrelevant to all those being copied, delete
those from the cc, or start another thread.
o Copy your direct manager on all emails. When you need to copy other
people on an email, it should be clear why they are copied even if it is
simply ‘for information’, and if action is required from any recipient that
they should be in the ‘To’ address field.
o The Executive Director shall not be kept in the cc of day-to-day work
emails unless otherwise requested. He shall only be kept in the cc of the
emails that are on the organization level and in the emails that he should
be informed about, Examples for such emails are:
•
General announcements by any of the departments.
•
When the Executive Director is the employee’s Direct Manger, and
his approval or information is required.
•
Some communication with Donors and partners when the presence
of the senior management is required.
o If you really need to know if an email has been received and read, ask
for confirmation, and/or add read receipt within the email settings.
o It is encouraged to use means other than an email, like phone or team
chat, when a subject or message does not require follow up or is just for
clarification.
o Do not circulate emails without checking with the sender and asking
permission to do so. As a form of communication, emails are considered
the property of the person composing them.

nodes.path: Section 02 > 2.3 Emails > Email Size and Security
nodes.heading: Email Size and Security
nodes.own_text:
o Before sending an attachment check whether it may be more effective
to put the content in the email itself, so that recipients can easily read it.
o If you have to send attachments, identify as clearly as possible which
attachments are being sent.

o If you need to attach large documents, files or images to your email make
sure they can still be delivered or received. GHD|EMPHNET has set a
maximum attachment size of 10Mb when sending or receiving. Files
larger than 10Mb still can be shared using Microsoft OneDrive. Caution
on sending large files externally as the recipient might not be able to
receive large files.
o Viruses can be contained in attachments to email messages. Malware is
a general term applied to electronic threats often transmitted by email or
by accessing some internet sites. You should be very careful about
opening email attachments, particularly if they are not from a known or
trusted email source. In addition to attachments, do not click links in
unsolicited or suspicious emails.
o Any virus incidents should be reported immediately to the Technology
and Innovative Solutions Department.

nodes.heading: 2.4. WhatsApp
nodes.own_text:
–HQ & Offices Group
Audience
GHD|EMPHNET employees at Headquarters and Country
Offices.
Purpose
This group is to serve as a convenient way for
GHD|EMPHNET’s team members to share knowledge,
communicate easily and efficiently regarding work-related
matters, and to exchange important and necessary
information related to the latest local, regional, and global
matters. This information will provide value and benefit to
the organization and its employees. Information shared
should fall with GHD|EMPHNET’s social media related
policies mentioned in the code of conduct and respecting the
privacy of the group members should always be maintained.
Best For
Exchange important and necessary information in relevant
to the latest local, regional, and global matters, share
events-related
information,
and
share
general
announcements.
Responsibility
➢ It is the responsibility of the Human Resources team to
add members once they join the organization and
remove members upon contract end/ resignation.
➢ It is the responsibility of all employees to share work
related information and to adhere to the WhatsApp
group policy.
➢ Membership is mandatory for all current members of
GHD|EMPHNET’s team as this group is a channel of
internal communication.
➢ New members should be added to the group within two
days of their employment at GHD|EMPHNET.

➢ Former employee will be removed from the group within
one week of their last working day.
➢ All members shall be committed to the WhatsApp group
policy mentioned below.
General instructions for GHD|EMPHNET WhatsApp group
Members should share work-related content, as well as exchange important
and necessary information that is relevant to latest local, regional, and global
matters. This includes but is not limited to reports, guidelines, news reports, and
GHD|EMPHNET’s conducted activities with photos (5 to 6 photos maximum per
event).
Do not have a one-on-one conversation in the group, should a one-on-one
conversation arise, consider continuing to private messages.
Make sure to avoid sending:
o Jokes.
o Memes.
o Unrelated content.
o Fake news.
o Political or religious opinions.
o Indecent content.
The HR team will be solely responsible for sharing and sending social events
related to the team on the WhatsApp group such as:
o Congratulations on academic/career achievements.
o Newborn baby wishes.
o Wedding wishes.
o Condolence messages for first & second-degree relatives only.
The discussions will be moderated by the group admin (HR Manager).
Any inappropriate messages that do not adhere to the group policy will be
removed.
Alternative groups or chats should be used for personal discussions or for organizing
social activities not related to the organization.

nodes.heading: Section 03: GHD|EMPHNET Internal Communication Matrix
nodes.note: short pointer section; the actual matrix content lives in Appendix 01
nodes.own_text:
x
Part of the organizational governance mandate is to set and manage internal
communication and periodic reporting for organization in order to manage its
operations and processes, take decisions, and control information flow efficiently
between different levels across the organization.
Appendix 01 provides an Internal Communication Matrix that demonstrates how
EMPHNET communicates internally, the kind of information that is communicated,
reports that are shared, and decisions that are disseminated. It also determines
the persons with authority to speak/ communicate on behalf of the different teams.
The communication matrix defines the following:
• Audience(s): the target for the communication, generally a function, unit,
leadership, individual, or group.
• Key Messages/ Purpose: the message to be shared. Primary messages and
purpose of the communication.
• Medium: the mechanism that will be used to deliver the communication, for
example, e-mail, newsletter article, Microsoft Teams, quarterly newsletter,
project status report, etc.
• Owner of Communication: who will create the content.
• Timing/ Frequency: proposed occurrence for planned communication.
Frequency (if a recurring communication) or number of communications
required.

nodes.path: Section 04 > Departmental and Teams bi-weekly meetings
nodes.heading: Departmental and Teams bi-weekly meetings
nodes.own_text:
gs
Each department, country office, team, or different teams across
departments meets on a bi-weekly basis to go over the work progress
assigned including:
o Description on progress made.
o Description of planned activities for the coming two weeks.
o Risks and issues that might impede progress.
Employees at the country offices are to be invited to attend this meeting
based on their relevancy to the meeting. Engaging the country offices
employees is essential in strengthening the communications between
Headquarters and the country.
Meeting minutes shall be documented using Minutes of Meeting (MoM)
template (Template 01) by the assigned person within one working day. After
taking the Direct Manager’s approval, it shall be shared with the attendees
keeping the Executive Director Secretary in the cc. In the upcoming meeting,
action points from the previous meeting shall be discussed and progress
shall be updated.
Each meetings schedule shall be shared with the Executive Office, and it will
be subject to monitoring by the Quality Management Unit.

nodes.heading: Executive Director’s bi-weekly meetings
nodes.own_text:
gs.
The Executive Director meets each senior team members who report to him
individually on a bi-weekly basis to go through their work progress, discuss
any issues/risks and raise any pending decision/actions required for the
relevant department/ tasks.
Senior team members shall share the discussion points one day before the
meeting and share the MoM one day after the meeting.

nodes.heading: Monthly Technical Day
nodes.own_text:
ay;
This meeting occurs on the first Saturday of each month, where a technical
topic is presented by a guest speaker followed by two presentations on
pertinent technical topics from the Center of Excellence for Applied
Epidemiology (CEAE) and another two topics from the Public Health
Programs (PHP). Held virtually, this meeting is attended by all technical team
members, country representatives, and focal points, Project Management
Office, Partnership and Resources Mobilization, Media and Communication,
Knowledge Exchange Team, and is left optional for other employees to
attend.
Refer to “ML-EXE-01 Executive Office Management Policies & Procedures
Manual” for more details.

nodes.heading: Quarterly Staff Meeting
nodes.own_text:
ng;

This meeting occurs every three months, to share updates at organizational
level, highlighting achievements, announcing new projects and partnerships,
welcoming new staff, providing an overview of the organization’s strategy
and seeking feedback from staff, and discussing any organization related
issues that need to be raised. Attending this meeting is mandatory for
Headquarters and Country Office employees.
The Human Resources team is the task owner for the quarterly staff meeting.
They are responsible for the planning, preparation, implementation and
reporting of the meeting. Invitations shall be shared within two weeks from
the meeting and the report shall be shared within two weeks of the meeting
conducted.
Staff meeting takes place in March, June and September. Conducting
EMPHNET Annual Meeting in December substitutes conducting staff
meeting.

nodes.heading: EMPHNET Annual Meeting
nodes.own_text:
ng;
This meeting is targeting all employees (Headquarters and Country Offices)
where senior management presents updates about organization’s strategy,
scope (areas of expertise and working areas), Human Resources and other
topics that all staff should be aware of and interested in.
A committee assigned by the Executive Director will be responsible for
planning, preparation, implementation and reporting on the meeting.
Invitations shall be shared within one month from the meeting and the report
shall be shared within two weeks of the meeting’s conclusion.
The annual meeting takes place in December.

nodes.heading: Senior Management Team Meeting
nodes.own_text:
ng.
The Executive Director meets the senior management team on a bi-weekly
basis to discuss high level matters related to strategic project/program,
partnership, new opportunities, organizational development, etc.
In addition, this meeting will be conducted Quarterly where Country Offices
Managers will be invited. This meeting aims to discuss the high-level matters
for related to the Country Offices. This meeting is conducted in March, June,
September and December.
This meeting is planned, prepared and reported on by the Executive Director
Office representative.

nodes.heading: Quarterly Strategy Meeting
nodes.own_text:
ng;
This meeting is essential to follow up on the strategy performance and
progress, making sure it is a live document and that concerned teams and
directors are working towards achieving their strategic objectives and
approaches and are committed to the Monitoring and Evaluation plan.

nodes.heading: Quarterly Management Meeting
nodes.next_heading: Monthly HQ Country Team and the Country Office Employees' Meeting
nodes.own_text:
ng
Project Management Office (PMO), technical, and sometimes finance teams
meet on a quarterly basis to revise the Gantt chart and deal with any problems
related to the timeline, scope, budget of a project, and they make any
necessary changes that have significant or strategic impact on projects.

nodes.path: Section 04 > Monthly HQ Country Team and the Country Office Employees' Meeting
nodes.heading: Monthly HQ Country Team and the Country Office Employees’ Meeting
nodes.own_text:
ing;
In addition to the technical participation of the country office team in the HQ
biweekly meetings, each HQ Country team shall meet with the Country Office
employees, on a monthly basis, to discuss administrative and management
related topics, discuss any issues/risks, and raise any pending decision/
actions required.
